savings.reason: Reading record LSP-EO_12379 (EO 12379, 47 FR 36099-36100, read once in full): no savings, continuation, transfer or exception provision anywhere in secs. 1-25; sec. 16 revokes EO 12089 'as amended' without qualification, so the revocation also reaches the amendment (EO 12107 sec. 2-101). Own-residual check, reading EO 12089 in full: it created a coordinating Council of agency heads with coordination, policy-issue and liaison functions and administrative provisions. It conferred no right or benefit, transferred no function, property or funds, and set no duty that outlives the Council. The U.S. Code note at 15 U.S.C. 2401 note records the revocation and no saving. S0 prefill (none_after_bounded_search) KEPT. Bounded search: EO 12089 and EO 12379 in full, plus the amending section of EO 12107 (2-101, list of orders, 44 FR 1055-1058).

research_rationale: EO 12089 (signed October 23, 1978; 43 FR 49773-49774), read in full from the held FR text, created the National Productivity Council with no term or sunset. EO 12107 sec. 2-101 (signed December 28, 1978; 44 FR 1055), read in the held FR text, lists EO 12089 among the orders in which 'Civil Service Commission' is replaced by 'Office of Personnel Management'; this is a partial amendment of the membership list in 1-102(i), not an ending. The dossier holds no located ACT record for EO 12107 ('target provision not located'), so it is described in the 1-102 clause reason rather than attached as a later event. EO 12379 sec. 16 (August 17, 1982; 47 FR 36099-36100), read in full, revokes 'Executive Order No. 12089, as amended' and states no effective date, so it took effect on signing. The dossier's segmentation was incomplete (item (j) absorbed everything to the end), so I replaced it with 12 section-level scopes covering every operative paragraph. Earlier-end test: the OFR catalog (3 hits), U.S. Code (15 U.S.C. 2401 note) and eCFR hits show only the 12107 amendment and the 12379 revocation; no other order ended or superseded the Council before 1982.
